new.title: Step inside the Kaymakamlar Mansion museum
new.desc: The Kaymakamlar Müze Evi is a restored Safranbolu konak that stages 18th and 19th century household life with figures in period rooms. It shows the layout of a typical Ottoman family house with separate men's and women's quarters.
new.tip: Allow about 40 minutes; it sits a short walk uphill from the Çarşı.
new.q: Kaymakamlar Müze Evi, Kaymakamlar Sk, Çarşı, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Tour Mümtazlar Konağı, a restored Safranbolu mansion
new.desc: Mümtazlar Konağı is one of the restored Safranbolu mansions open to visitors, listed by the Ministry of Culture among the town's well-known houses. It is furnished to show how a wealthy Ottoman family lived.
new.tip: Combine it with nearby houses; hours are shorter in winter.

new.title: Visit the Safranbolu City History Museum
new.desc: The museum occupies the former government building, built in 1906 and used by the administration until 1976. Restored and opened as a museum in 2006, it presents the town's past through displays on trades and daily life.
new.tip: It is on the main square at the heart of the Çarşı, so it fits between other stops.
new.q: Safranbolu Kent Tarihi Müzesi, Hükümet Sokak, Çeşme, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Admire the 17th-century Cinci Han caravanserai
new.desc: Cinci Hoca Hanı is a 17th-century caravanserai built by the judge Cinci Hoca, with a stone ground floor and a wooden upper storey around a courtyard. It is the best-known building of the Çarşı.
new.tip: The upper floor and roof terrace give views of the old town's tiled roofs.

new.title: Take a scrub at the Cinci Hamam
new.desc: Cinci Hamam was built by Cinci Hoca in the 17th century next to his caravanserai and still works as a traditional Turkish bath. It has a domed cold room and a heated marble hot room.
new.tip: Bring your own towel or rent one; mornings are quietest.

new.title: See the Köprülü Mehmet Paşa Mosque and its sundial
new.desc: Built in 1661-62 by Grand Vizier Köprülü Mehmet Pasha, this is the largest mosque in Safranbolu. Its courtyard holds a marble sundial and a fountain.
new.tip: Visit between prayer times and dress modestly.
new.q: Köprülü Mehmet Paşa Camii, Çarşı, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Watch sunset from Hıdırlık Hill
new.desc: Hıdırlık Tepesi overlooks the old town's tiled roofs and is traditionally where early Turks held rain prayers and the Hıdırellez spring festival. It has a small park and a cafe.
new.tip: Walk up from the Çarşı in about 15 minutes; sunset is best.
new.q: Hıdırlık Tepesi, Hıdırlık Sk, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Shop for yemeni shoes in the Yemeniciler Arastası
new.desc: The Arasta bazaar was home to the makers of yemeni, the soft flat-heeled leather shoes of Safranbolu. Today most stalls sell crafts, though a workshop still produces the shoes.
new.tip: Ask for genuine leather and check the stitching.
new.q: Yemeniciler Arastası, Arasta Sokak, Çeşme, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Eat bükme and kuyu kebabı at Kadıoğlu Şehzade Sofrası
new.desc: Kadıoğlu Şehzade Sofrası is a Çarşı restaurant known for bükme, a covered spinach pide, and kuyu kebabı. The menu is built around Safranbolu home cooking.
new.tip: Order bükme with ayran; it is inexpensive.
new.q: Kadıoğlu Şehzade Sofrası, Arasta Sk, Çarşı, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Buy Safranbolu lokum at İmren Lokumları
new.desc: İmren is a Safranbolu lokum maker known for its saffron and mastic (sakızlı) Turkish delight; Safranbolu lokum holds a geographical indication. The shop sells it by weight.
new.tip: Ask to taste the saffron variety before buying.
new.q: İmren Lokumları, Cinci Han Sokak, Çeşme, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Eat saffron-scented köfte at Şehr-i Safran Köftecisi
new.desc: A family-run köfte restaurant in Safranbolu's old bazaar, serving lamb or beef meatballs with salad and pita or rice. Diners also mention saffron rice and other Safranbolu dishes.
new.tip: Ask for the köfte with pilav and winter salad. It is tucked into the lanes behind Cinci Han, so look for Han Arkası Sokak.
new.q: Şehr-i Safran Köftecisi, Han Arkası Sokak 14, Musalla, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: See the İncekaya Aqueduct above the canyon
new.desc: The six-arch, 116 m İncekaya Aqueduct crosses a side branch of the Tokatlı canyon and was renewed by Grand Vizier İzzet Mehmet Pasha, with repairs in the 1790s. It is on the road to the glass terrace.
new.tip: Go in the morning for the best light.

new.title: Step onto the Tokatlı Canyon glass terrace
new.desc: The Kristal Teras hangs 80 m above Tokatlı Canyon, 11 m wide with three 3 cm glass sections rated to 75 tonnes. The canyon runs about 9 km from Tokatlı village.
new.tip: Tickets are bought on site; avoid summer weekends.
new.q: Kristal Teras, Tokatlı Kanyonu, Safranbolu, Karabük

new.title: Walk into Bulak Mencilis Cave
new.desc: Bulak Mencilis is a 6.5 km hydrologically active cave about 7 km from Safranbolu, of which roughly 400 m is open as a walkway. It is the fourth largest cave of Türkiye.
new.tip: Wear shoes with grip; it stays cool inside.

new.title: Wander Yörük Village's stone lanes
new.desc: Yörük Village east of Safranbolu preserves old Ottoman village houses and is a stop on many Safranbolu itineraries. It has tea houses and a small museum.
new.tip: Visit by car or taxi from the Çarşı.

new.title: Explore the Roman ruins of Hadrianopolis
new.desc: Hadrianopolis, about 3 km west of Eskipazar, was a Roman and Byzantine city in Paphlagonia with baths, water channels and a church complex under excavation. It is nicknamed the Zeugma of the Black Sea for its mosaics.
new.tip: Check opening times; some mosaics are covered.

new.title: Climb Kastamonu Castle for the city view
new.desc: Kastamonu Castle rises above the old town in Atabeygazi quarter, a medieval fortress attributed to the Komnenoi and the historical core of the city. Its walls and towers remain.
new.tip: Go at sunset when the roofs below glow.

new.title: Visit the Nasrullah Kadı Mosque and fountain square
new.desc: The Nasrullah Kadı Mosque, built in the early 18th century, anchors Kastamonu's central Nasrullah Square with its Ottoman-era fountain. It is a landmark of the old city core.
new.tip: Pair it with tea in the square.
new.q: Nasrullah Kadı Camii, Nasrullah Meydanı, Kastamonu

new.title: Tour the Ethnography Museum in Liva Paşa Mansion
new.desc: The Kastamonu Ethnography Museum has been in the Liva Paşa Mansion, built around 1870-1887, since 1997. It shows local costume, crafts and house life.
new.tip: Allow 45 minutes.
new.q: Kastamonu Etnografya Müzesi, Liva Paşa Konağı, Kastamonu

new.title: See the 1443 Kurşunlu Han and İsmail Bey complex
new.desc: Kurşunlu Han, built in 1443 as part of the İsmail Bey complex, sits below the castle rock with two ancient rock tombs. It is now a hotel but its courtyard can be seen.
new.tip: Ask at reception to look around.

new.title: Pay respects at Şeyh Şaban-ı Veli Complex
new.desc: The complex holds the tomb of the Halveti saint Şeyh Şaban-ı Veli (16th century), with a mosque, fountain and museum. It is a major pilgrimage site in Kastamonu.
new.tip: Dress modestly and come outside prayer times.
new.q: Şeyh Şaban-ı Veli Külliyesi, Kastamonu merkez, Kastamonu

new.title: Order etli ekmek at Tiryakioğlu
new.desc: Tiryakioğlu is a Kastamonu etli ekmek place rated highly by diners. Kastamonu's version is thicker and round, unlike Konya's long thin one.
new.tip: Eat it hot with ayran.
new.q: Tiryakioğlu Etli Ekmek, Adalet Cd, Hepkebirler, Kastamonu

new.title: Visit the wooden Mahmut Bey Mosque in Kasaba
new.desc: Built in 1366 by Mahmut Bey, brother of the Candaroğlu ruler Kötürüm Bayezid, this wooden-pillared mosque is on UNESCO's tentative list, with old hamams in the village. It is about 15 km from Kastamonu on the Daday road.
new.tip: Ask in the village for the key.

new.title: See the ruins of Pompeiopolis near Taşköprü
new.desc: Pompeiopolis was a Paphlagonian city near Taşköprü, founded under Pompey and known for its mound and theatre remains.
new.tip: Combine it with Taşköprü's garlic market.

new.title: Walk İnebolu's Ottoman slate-stone houses
new.desc: İnebolu's seafront streets are lined with historic Ottoman houses built in slate stone, in the port where supplies entered Anatolia during the War of Independence.
new.tip: Stroll to the harbour for tea.

new.title: Hike the Horma Canyon walkway
new.desc: Horma Canyon in Pınarbaşı, Küre Mountains National Park, has a footpath through its first stretch and ends at Ilıca Waterfall. It is milder than Valla Canyon.
new.tip: Go with a guide in wet weather.

new.title: Cool off at Ilıca Waterfall
new.desc: Ilıca Waterfall drops about 15 m into a natural pool where the Horma Canyon ends, beside the ruins of a Byzantine-era bath.
new.tip: Best visited in summer.

new.title: Descend toward Ilgarini Cave
new.desc: Ilgarini Cave near Pınarbaşı is about 850 m long and 250 m deep, Türkiye's fourth-deepest, reached by a steep forest slope.
new.tip: Only for experienced cavers with a guide.

new.title: Look into the depths of Valla Canyon
new.desc: Valla Canyon is among the deepest in the world; a full crossing needs permission, a guide and gear, but viewpoints exist.
new.tip: Book a licensed guide.

new.title: Walk the Ersizlerdere Canyon nature park
new.desc: Ersizlerdere Nature Park lies in the Küre district inside Küre Mountains National Park. Forest trails lead to canyon viewpoints, and picnic areas are set out along the way; autumn colours are the highlight.
new.tip: Bring food and water, as little is sold on site. Spring and autumn are the best seasons, and trails can be rocky.

new.title: Walk up to Amasra Castle on Boztepe
new.desc: Amasra's cut-stone castle on Boztepe was added to UNESCO's tentative list in 2013, reached over an ancient bridge.
new.tip: Come at sunset.

new.title: Enter the Bedesten, Amasra's Roman basilica
new.desc: The Bedesten is described as the ancient heart of Amasra and was a Roman basilica. Entry is free.
new.tip: A quick stop in the centre.

new.title: Visit the Amasra Museum
new.desc: The museum is in an 1884 building that began as a maritime school, holding finds from ancient Amastris.
new.tip: Allow 30 minutes.

new.title: Cross the Roman Kemere Bridge to Boztepe
new.desc: The Roman Kemere Bridge connects the town to Boztepe island and is a symbol of Bartın.
new.tip: Walk it at dusk.

new.title: Browse the Çekiciler Çarşısı
new.desc: Amasra's market lane sells local pastırma, cheese, dried figs and honey.
new.tip: Taste before you buy.

new.title: See the Roman Kuşkayası road monument
new.desc: A Roman rock-cut monument with a human figure, an eagle and two inscriptions, about 4 km from Amasra.
new.tip: Quiet and free.
new.q: Kuşkayası Yol Anıtı, Gömü, Amasra, Bartın

new.title: Eat Amasra salad at Amasra Sofrası
new.desc: Amasra Sofrası is among restaurants guides name for Amasra salad, said to use some 30 ingredients with pomegranate syrup.
new.tip: Order it with fresh fish.
new.q: Amasra Sofrası, Hamam Sk, Kum, Amasra, Bartın

new.title: Order fish at Çınar Balık Restaurant
new.desc: Çınar Balık is named by guides for Amasra salad served with the day's fish.
new.tip: Ask for the catch of the day.

new.title: Visit Ulukaya Waterfall near Ulus
new.desc: Ulukaya Waterfall is in Ulukaya Village, 17 km from Ulus.
new.tip: Best in the dry season.

new.title: Tour Gökgöl Cave
new.desc: Gökgöl is a show cave opened to visitors in 2001, one of Türkiye's largest.
new.tip: Cool inside, bring a jacket.

new.title: Walk the ancient city of Tios at Filyos
new.desc: Tios (Tieion) in Filyos was founded by Milesian colonists and traded between Bithynia and Paphlagonia; excavations began in 2006.
new.tip: Includes the castle hill.
new.q: Tios Antik Kenti, Filyos, Çaycuma, Zonguldak

new.title: Descend into the Zonguldak Mining Museum
new.desc: A coal mine converted into the first mine museum in Türkiye.
new.tip: Book ahead.
